titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 47: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 47. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: Six dots and a closing bracket (708–712) with no opening bracket; the dots are illegible and the bracket an unpaired sign (ledger §4).

The framed manuscript page number [ⲙⲍ] (top right) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame; the running title [ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ] is restored, with a stroke over ⲙ. Illegible dots: six before the bracket (567–699), four after it (734–813), five after ϩ (876–982), three after ⲡⲱ (1162–1216), two after ⲏ (1274, 1301), three at the line end (1359–1411). No strokes. Reconcile flags on ll. 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 13–16, 18, 25, 27–32 are explained by dots of area < 6 and by dot rows standing at the zone centre (top ≤ centre + 1, ll. 2, 16, 18, 27, 29, 30, 32), which it does not count; on l. 11 it also counts a speck of the German "abgerieben" (1254), on l. 34 the dots of the German statement. Every dot was counted on the 4× sheets.
Five dots and a closing bracket (682–686) with no opening bracket; unpaired sign (as l. 1).

Illegible dots: five before the bracket (566–673), two after ⲕⲱ (756, 782), six after ϩ ⲡ (877–1009), three after ⲁⲡ (1170–1223), one after ⲉⲧ (1320), three at the line end (1370–1411, set closer, 20 px). Dots under ⲱ of ⲕⲱ (729) and ⲛ (1345). No strokes.
"leer" after the dots → vac.; ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲩⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ begins with an enlarged ⲡ in mid-line.

Two dots inside the brackets (575, 602), two after them (637, 663), three after ⲡⲣ (1182–1235). A dot under the enlarged ⲡ, between its legs (801, y 417, area 3, 6×). Dots under ⲙ, ⲟ, ⲩ, ⲧ of ⲡⲉⲧⲟⲩⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ (899–950) and the final ⲡ (1404). Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁϥ (1261–1273); the strokes tool also reports the descender of ⲣ of l. 2 (1052–1060).

Dots under ⲣ (628, left of the descender), ⲛ (680), ⲡ (803), ⲏ (883), ⲟ, ⲩ, ⲓ, ⲉ of ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲓⲉⲩⲉ (1157–1197) and ϩ of ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ (1326). Diaeresis over ⲓ of ⲡϫⲁⲓ (1067/1073). Strokes over ⲙ after the bracket (971–984), and two separate bars over ⲛ (1096–1108) and the first ⲙ (1115–1128) of ⲛⲙⲙⲟⲩⲓⲉⲩⲉ.
The restoration [...ⲟⲩⲁ] holds three dots (575–616) followed by restored letters.
